name: Analogue Space
task: Unsupervised: group Earth's land into environment types and place Moon/Mars targets among them.

data.earth: 354,342 land cells of 0.25° (about 28 km) from the Analog Finder grid: NASA MODIS MOD11C3 land surface temperature, MOD13C2 NDVI, MCD43C3 albedo (2024), JAXA AW3D30 elevation.
data.targets: 16 Moon and Mars Finder targets from LRO Diviner/LOLA and Mars Odyssey GRS/NS, MGS TES and MOLA, translated into Earth units the same way the Finder does (role dimensions by rank).

method: Standardise each of the 7 features with area-weighted mean and standard deviation (cells near the poles are smaller).
PCA on the area-weighted covariance matrix; the 2D chart shows PC1 and PC2.
Weighted k-means (k-means++ seeding, best of 6 restarts) with k = 8, fitted on 60,000 area-weighted cells and applied to every cell.
Each type is named from its centroid's physical values (temperature, vegetation, freezing, relief, swing), never from geography.
Moon and Mars targets are mapped into the same standardised space; features a target lacks sit at Earth's mean.

score.label: Cluster stability
score.text: Adjusted Rand index 0.86 ± 0.12 across 10 bootstrap re-fits (1 = identical types every time). PC1 and PC2 hold 77 % of the variance.

limits: Seven climate-and-terrain features only: no chemistry, mineralogy, radar roughness or dust.
Moon and Mars targets lie far outside Earth's range on temperature, so they sit at the edge of the cloud; the nearest type says which Earth environment is least unlike them, not that it matches.
k = 8 is a readable choice, not a natural number of environments: the k scan shows no sharp elbow.
0.25° cells blend small features (a crater, a dry valley) with their surroundings.
MODIS observes at about 10:30 and 22:30, so the day–night swing understates the true daily range.
